chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father. He said:

I spoke to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), describing the worship, religion, and virtue of a certain person as being such-and-such. So he said: "How is his intellect?" So I said: "I do not know." So he said: "Indeed, reward is according to the measure of intellect.

Indeed, a man from the Children of Israel used to worship God, Mighty and Majestic, on a green, verdant island abundant in trees and pure of water among the islands of the sea. An angel passed by him and said: 'O Lord, show me the reward of this servant of Yours.' God showed him that, and the angel considered it small. God revealed to him: 'Accompany him.' The angel came to him in human form and said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am a worshiper. We heard of your place and worship here, so I came to worship God with you.' He stayed with him that day. When morning came, the angel said: 'Your place is indeed a retreat.' He said: 'If only our Lord had a beast. If our Lord had a donkey, we would herd it here, for this grass goes to waste.' The angel said: 'Does your Lord not have a donkey?' He said: 'If He had a donkey, this grass would not go to waste.' God revealed to the angel: 'I only reward him according to the measure of his intellect.'

And al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) never spoke to the worshipers at the full extent of his own intellect." He said: And the Messenger of God said: "We, the company of prophets, were commanded to speak to people at the level of their intellects."

key_terms.الثواب: Divine reward -- tied to the level of intellect
key_terms.العقل: Intellect, reason -- the faculty that determines the quality and value of worship
key_terms.بهيمة: Beast of burden -- the worshiper's wish reveals his anthropomorphic conception of God
key_terms.كنه: The full depth, essence -- used regarding the Prophet's intellect

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intellect and divine reward in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that divine reward is proportional to one's intellect, not merely the quantity of worship. He illustrates this with the story of a devout Israelite worshiper living on a lush island who, despite his piety, wished that God had a donkey to graze on the island's grass -- revealing a fundamentally flawed understanding of God's nature. The hadith concludes with the prophetic principle that prophets were commanded to communicate with people according to their intellectual capacity.
